semantics: The original function computes a fixed-stride record inside the object and checks record+4 for nonzero before updating a ring-like cursor/count substructure at record+16.

For the nonzero branch, it adds R6 to substructure+20 (position), wraps against substructure+8 by subtracting substructure+4, clears associated fields at wrap/thresholds, subtracts R6 from substructure+48 (remaining), and adds R6 to substructure+44 (total).
The caller selects the record index from original_object+0x3c64 and forwards its own R5 input as this routine R6. The sampled increment is zero.

The same update routine is also used by an adjacent MPEG demux wrapper (call0x8c2efb4e), with its index sourced from object+0x2fe4; that adjacency/shared routine alone does not identify the sampled record as audio or video.
supported: PC and PR are coherent with a valid original call and valid in-RAM indexed record address.
The postmultiply R5 is reproduced by index2 (uniquely modulo2^29), and the original fixed-stride calculation reproduces sampled R4 exactly. The original index high3bits are not captured.
This differs from the earlier C29 interrupt sample at MPEG parser entry0x8c3306c2.
limits: This is a single interrupt-time sample at intentional diagnostic stop, not a fault address or proof of a stalled instruction.
The live record+4 and all ring state are not captured. No read success, decode success, rendering success, frame publication or specific audio/video ownership follows.
A zero update increment at this instant is legal for this bounded code and does not by itself prove a repeating zero-progress loop.
